events.title: A Gift in Motion
events.description: A multidisciplinary showcase from the artists and scholars of the full-time faculty and staff at the Corcoran School of the Arts & Design. A Gift In Motion loosely draws from Robin Wall Kimmerer’s book The Serviceberry which uplifts Indigenous frameworks of the natural world to advance the possibilities in collectivity, reciprocity, and the mindset of abundance. These are anti-capitalist models and theories that provide insight into the systems of power we negotiate, but also offer a lens on how we individually move through our daily lives—together—through historically fraught landscapes. A keen reminder that working with, for, and because of each other remains the most human motivation, even while we are inundated with narratives that suggest otherwise. Within the walls of the academy, frameworks of artistic and creative knowledge are often dismissed, as are Indigenous methodologies and community-focused perspectives that center human engagement, oral and craft-based practices, and unquantifiable research. A personal experience. A feeling. Abstraction. And yet, for centuries, within the walls of art schools exist myriad economies of imagination that are anchored in the sharing of diverse creative knowledge and articulated in what we make, write, perform, dance, build, conserve, collect, display, speak, and think. events.title: Bison: Standing Strong
events.address: 10th St. & Constitution Ave., NW, Washington, DC 20560
events.description: Explore the remarkable story of bison. These iconic animals shaped North American landscapes for more than 100,000 years and anchored Indigenous lifeways for generations. Pushed to the brink of extinction in the 19th century, bison survived thanks to dedicated conservation efforts. Today, they stand strong as an enduring symbol of survival and resilience. The Bison: Standing Strong exhibit invites you into this incredible journey. Explore a full-sized bull bison specimen, the six-foot-wide skull of an ancient bison ancestor, an immersive soundscape, multimedia, cutting-edge scientific research, and Native objects and stories shared in collaboration with community members. Experience the deep history of America’s national mammal and discover the hopeful future being built for generations to come.

events.title: Bronze Bison: Exhibit
events.address: 10th St. & Constitution Ave., NW, Washington, DC 20560
events.description: More than 100 years ago, real bison grazed outside the Smithsonian Castle building. Bison are returning in a bold new way! Three larger-than-life bronze bison, created by sculptor Gary Staab, find a permanent home outside the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History. These towering sculptures of a bull, cow, and calf are at 125 percent scale and modeled after taxidermy specimens seen at the Smithsonian between 1888 and 1957. The original bison diorama introduced generations of visitors to an animal and a prairie landscape they had never seen and helped spark the bison conservation movement. The new bison bronzes will welcome visitors from around the world and celebrate America’s national mammal. Gift of Naoma Tate and the family of Hal Tate.

events.title: Camelot
events.description: Welcome to CAMELOT! Borrowing from the Arthurian legends, CAMELOT is Lerner and Loewe's fantastical masterpiece. An idealistic King Arthur hopes to create a kingdom built on honor and dignity, embodied by his Knights of The Round Table. He establishes an order built on using “might for right.” His ideals, however, are tested when his lovely queen, Guenevere, falls in love with his most loyal knight, Lancelot. Add in the dastardly Mordred and his wicked schemes and it soon appears this dream of a kingdom may only exist for one brief, shining moment. ​ This stirring Golden Age musical has enchanted generations of theatregoers with its sweeping score and iconic characters. It is a romance, a tragedy, a comedy, an adventure, a fantasy, and a stirring exploration of power and leadership all at once. And above all, it is a piece about the stories and ideals we pass along to future generations.​

events.title: Cannupa Hanska Luger’s REFLECT
events.description: REFLECT traces the evolution of artist Cannuap Hanska Luger’s Mirror Shield Project. In 2016, when the Dakota Access Pipeline threatened the waters of his ancestral homelands, Luger circulated a video demonstrating how to make “mirror shields” from inexpensive materials. Conceived during the Indigenous-led resistance at Standing Rock, North Dakota, the tutorial functioned as a call to collective action, an invitation for people across the country to stand in solidarity with the Water Protectors. Carried by Water Protectors in frontline actions and collective formations, the mirrored surfaces offered protection while redirecting the field of vision. More than a thousand mirror shields were created and transported to the Očhéthi Šakówiŋ camp. The exhibition brings the project’s history into the present, treating the archive as a resource to be carried forward and put into practice. Photographs, videos, garments, ephemera, and community-generated documentation reveal a collective artwork shaped by those who made, carried, adapted, interpreted, and activated it.

events.title: Civil War History in Oakton and Vienna
events.description: Greater Oakton Community Association invites history enthusiasts to join a narrated historic bus tour led by acclaimed local historian Jim Lewis on from 9:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. Please arrive at 9:00 a.m. at Oakton Community Park at 2841 Hunter Mill Road (next to the old schoolhouse and roundabout) for Jim Lewis's opening comments, then board the bus for departure by 9:30 a.m. The tour will end at 1:00 p.m. This 3.5-hour journey spans Fairfax County's history from its formation in 1742 through the early 1900s, focusing on sites primarily on or just off Hunter Mill Road. Participants hear stories of where the old mills and roads were located and learn about famed military figures (particularly from the Civil War era) and colorful residents who graced the area. Numerous period photographs support the narrative, bringing history to life. Walking requirements are minimal, although one segment involves going down a slight grassy decline. The tour runs rain or shine. Snacks and water are included. Cost is $45 per seat. In the event of cancellation, refunds are provided if a replacement is found for the seat; a wait list is maintained for this purpose. There are 23 seats on the bus. Special "Event Pricing" is offered for the award-winning "Danger Between the Lines" DVD and tour-related illustrated books, available for purchase with cash only. Narrated Historic Bus Tour with Jim Lewis combines local history education, community connection, and immersive storytelling in Fairfax County, Virginia. Questions? Email contact@greateroakton.com . events.title: Cracks & Reforms: The 1920s Through the GW Collection
events.description: The 1920s emerged as a decade suspended between collapse and reconstruction, an era marked by “cracks and reforms” that ushered in a profound reconfiguration of the visual world. During this period marked by civil transformation and political upheaval, artists, journalists, and makers had opportunities to reconstruct both individual and collective identities. A century later, Cracks & Reforms presents a distinct cross-section of this period, revealing global currents of migration, modernization, and cultural redefinition through the lens of the GW Collection. Students led by Associate Professor Bibiana Obler selected works to study and exhibit, their research eventually leading to unified themes and a catalog designed by Corcoran graphic design students led by professors Sharmila Karamchandani and Aasawari Kulkarni. Image: Boris Ignatovich (Russian, 1899-1976), Composer Dmitri Shostakovich, from "Ignatovich, Soviet Avant-Garde", 1928, gelatin silver print, 16 H x 20 W in. Along the way, Anna teams up with rugged ice harvester Kristoff, his loyal reindeer Sven, and the ever-optimistic snowman Olaf in an adventure that tests the meaning of love, loyalty, and sacrifice. The musical includes beloved songs such as “Let It Go,” “Do You Want to Build a Snowman?” and “For the First Time in Forever,” alongside thrilling new numbers written exclusively for Broadway. A powerful tale of self-acceptance and the unbreakable strength of family, Frozen the Broadway Musical is a magical, uplifting experience for audiences of all ages. events.title: Entertainment Nation
events.address: 14th Street and Constitution Avenue, N.W., Washington, DC 20560
events.description: Entertainment has the power to captivate, inspire and transform us. It brings us together. We share it when we spontaneously recite lines from a favorite movie, dance to the same groove or recreate a national sports moment on a neighborhood street. It can also spur critical conversations, expose divides, and foster important historical change. Through the National Museum of American History’s extraordinary collection of theater, music, sports, movie and television objects, the exhibition features a powerful, ever-changing selection of objects and interactive experiences. Through the objects and their stories, the exhibition explores how, for more than 150 years, entertainment has provided a forum for important national conversations about who we are, and who we want to be.

events.title: Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY
events.description: For Freedoms presents artist and educator Eric Gottesman’s NIGHT AND DAY which centers on Ethiopian journalist and author Baalu Girma’s controversial 1984 Amharic novel Oromay, written under the Derg regime and banned shortly after its publication. Drawing on Gottesman’s deep engagement with the novel, NIGHT AND DAY considers how artists create, communicate, and sustain cultural memory within and against conditions of censorship, political repression, and state violence. The exhibition extends beyond the gallery through a library of banned books, a self-guided workshop station that invites visitors to respond to censorship through writing and drawing, and a public conversation on how artists sustain creative practice amid sociopolitical pressure.

Along the way, learn about the soldiers who lived and worked here and the challenges they faced while stationed in the field. At the fort, explore the earthworks that still stand today and imagine what life was like inside this military post. Rangers will share stories of daily routines, military strategy, and the experiences of those who served here. This hike offers a chance to experience history where it happened while connecting with the natural landscape that surrounds it. This program begins at the Rock Creek Park Nature Center.

After the film, three UMD faculty will talk about it from the angles of politics, history and cinema. About “14th” Written in the wreckage of the Civil War, the 14th Amendment was meant to close the door on the hierarchy of human worth. Instead, it has become a permanent argument. Ava DuVernay’s “14th” pulls this constitutional fight out of the footnotes and into the present, chronicling the vicious battle over the amendment that has raged for over 150 years. Threading deep archival scholarship with piercing headlines of today, “14th” brings together legal minds, politicians, historians and cultural voices in direct conversation with a question America still hasn’t settled: Who gets to belong? events.title: Friends Gather Here: A Legacy of Two Communities at Woodlawn
events.description: Friends Gather Here: A Legacy of Two Communities at Woodlawn explores the powerful history of Quaker families who came to Woodlawn to establish an antislavery community rooted in equality and nonviolence. Through innovative farming and free labor, they sought to demonstrate an alternative to slavery in Virginia, settling alongside a small, established free Black community already living in the area. This exhibit examines the parallel lives, shared aspirations, and evolving relationships between these neighboring communities. As part of the Virginia 250th commemoration, Friends Gather Here invites us to reflect on this quiet revolution and examine our nation’s foundational ideals. On View: June 27 – December 30, 2026 Admission: Free (with suggested donation)

events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

events.title: In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness
events.address: 14th Street and Constitution Avenue, N.W., Washington, DC 20560
events.description: The Smithsonian’s National Museum of American History will lead the nation’s 250th anniversary celebrations with a bold, immersive exhibition exploring the ideals of the Declaration of Independence. In Pursuit of Life, Liberty & Happiness will span three floors and 300,000 square feet, featuring 250 significant objects, including the desk Jefferson used to draft the Declaration of Independence. Another noteworthy artifact is the only surviving ship of the early U.S. Navy, the gunboat Philadelphia . This National Historic Landmark helped stall British forces and now will undergo an on-site conservation to preserve it for future generations. Visitors and online audiences can engage with both the triumphs and challenges of America’s journey through a year-long series of dynamic programs, from hands-on activities and theatrical performances to educational tools and virtual field trips for classrooms across the country. The museum's Semiquincentennial exhibitions and events begin in the spring of 2026, welcoming all Americans to reflect on the enduring and sometimes delayed or denied promises that surround the ongoing pursuit of life, liberty and happiness.

events.title: Indecent: The True Story of a Little Jewish Play
events.description: ASL Sign Interpreted Performance and Afterword discussion on Friday, November 20 . Written by Paula Vogel, Score and Original Music by Lisa Gutkin and Aaron Halva Directed by Sasha Olinick Performances will be held in the Theatre Arts Arena on the Montgomery College Rockville campus. In 1906 a young, up and coming Jewish/Polish writer, Sholem Asch, penned “God of Vengeance”, a play attacking religious hypocrisy and lovingly depicting a romantic relationship between two women. The play quickly became a hit as it toured throughout Europe and was translated from its original Yiddish into several different languages. But in America, when an English translation opened on Broadway in 1923, the play was quickly shut down and the cast, director and producer were jailed and prosecuted for violating obscenity laws. Indecent, by Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright Paula Vogel, charts the history of this incendiary drama and the path of the artists who risked their careers and lives to perform it. INDECENT is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Dramatists Play Service. Indecent is recommended for mature audiences and teenagers aged 13 and older due to adult themes and historical prejudice.

events.title: Les Misérables-Olney Theatre
events.description: Modern classics don’t come any bigger than Les Misérables, and Olney Theatre celebrates it for the first time in honor of the show’s 40th anniversary. Based on Victor Hugo’s sweeping 19th-century novel of redemption, revolution, and love, the songs of Les Miz conquered Broadway in the 1980s and continue to resonate in this third decade of the 21st Century. Follow Jean-Valjean from his beginnings as convict #24601 to life in hiding, to protector of Cosette, pursued all the while by the relentless Javert, culminating in the revolutionary passions of the 1832 Paris uprising. Join us at the barricade this holiday season, and be stirred by a musical unmatched by its lyrical humor, its calls for justice, and its portrayal of the sacrifices one can make in the name of love. events.title: Lonesome River Band
events.description: It’s hard to think of a genre more committed to sustained creative careers than bluegrass. Case in point: the 41-years-and-counting path of Mountain Home Music Company stalwarts, Lonesome River Band. Though the last remaining original member departed before the turn of the century, the group — a quintet for more than 20 years now — hasn’t so much reinvented itself as refined a profoundly influential signature sound that has a seemingly endless appeal to successive generations of fans and musicians alike. Led by 30-plus year veteran and award-winning banjo man Sammy Shelor, who has presided over one stellar lineup after another, LRB remains among the genre’s most widely admired and powerful draws, both in person and on streaming platforms.

events.title: Michael McDermott
events.description: Jammin' Java welcomes singer-songwriter Michael McDermott on Thursday, November 20th, 2026 at 7:00 p.m. at 227 Maple Avenue in Vienna, Fairfax County, Virginia. Chicago native McDermott has occupied a peculiar and essential place in American music for thirty-plus years: extravagantly praised by Stephen King, The Washington Post, and The Hollywood Reporter, yet perpetually on the verge of the recognition his artistry demands. Raised on the dual gospel of early Dylan and the Stones, Tom Waits and the Who, Woody Guthrie and Van Morrison, McDermott has never made a record that fits neatly into a marketing category—a restless refusal to be contained that makes him essential. His forthcoming album Flowers From The Graveyard (arriving August 21, 2027) collects 11 self-penned songs moving fluidly between anthemic rock and bruised introspection, between political fury and hard-won philosophical calm. The Hollywood Reporter notes "Despair never sounded so good," while Stephen King calls him "one of the best songwriters in the world." The Washington Post suggests "McDermott may prove to be one of his generation's greatest talents." This intimate performance delivers the uncompromising songwriting, raw emotional depth, and masterful artistry that define one of America's most important voices. Admission is $34.00 plus fees. Michael McDermott combines lyrical excellence, unflinching humanity, and timeless rock 'n' roll soul in Fairfax County, Virginia. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: Miguel Braceli: UNBURIAL (exhibition)
events.address: St. John's College, 60 College Avenue, Annapolis, MD 21401
events.description: Unburial treats absence as a site for learning and reflection. The void left by the Liberty Tree becomes more than metaphor: an art intervention transforms it into a place to be repurposed and reclaimed through rituals and celebrations that probe what freedom means today. On the front lawn, where the Liberty Tree once stood, the artist Miguel Braceli has installed a 40'-diameter circle of cemetery vases filled with common wildflowers. It calls attention to the tree's absence and reclaims it as a tree for all people, not just the privileged and elite (e.g., the Sons of Liberty and the four Annapolis signers of the Declaration of Independence). In the museum, Braceli, with the help of a team of fabricators, created three enormous murals and two other works. The murals perform an autopsy of the tree. The largest multiplies the tulip poplar's distinctive leaf shape across a 33'-long wall in a wind-swept swirl of energy (the leaves were made from stencils of the Liberty Tree scion's actual leaves). A second mural abstracts the tree's tangled root system into a water-bearing drawing (using PVC tubing) that sprouts purple carnations. The third mural's subject is the tree's massive trunk, which was cut to pieces in 1999, with much of the wood later finding commemorative as Liberty Tree guitars, conference tables, and bible boxes. Onto nine chalkboards, Braceli has mounted nine pieces of raw wood, each supporting live orchids. What can we learn anew from this tree?, it seems to ask. The two other works urge us to turn away from nation-state identities and to look and listen more closely to nature. A sculptural ear is mounted onto the red silhouette of a rose petal, borrowed from the work of Columbia-born, Venezuela-based artist Roberto Obregoń. Nearby, a flag of yellow roses hangs from a flagpole that has been fabricated from a branch. Admission & Hours Free & open to the public Wednesday, Thursday, Saturday, and Sunday, 10 a.m. to 6 p.m. Open Friday, 12 to 7:30 p.m. Parking

Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. events.title: New Players, Old Plays? Continuity and Change in Development Diplomacy
events.venue: School of Media and Public Affairs
events.description: Overview Are emerging powers reshaping international development cooperation or playing by the existing rules? Abstract The growing participation of emerging powers in international development cooperation raises questions about the changing nature of development diplomacy. As these actors expand their roles as donors, are they challenging established practices and structures, or reproducing them? More broadly, does the arrival of new actors necessarily change how development diplomacy is practiced and understood? This talk explores these questions through two ongoing research projects that examine the structural and communicative dimensions of development diplomacy. The first study, Claiming a Seat at the Table: Legitimacy Narratives of Emerging Donors in Development Diplomacy, examines how China, Saudi Arabia, and Turkey communicate their roles as development actors to general public. Through a quantitative content analysis of 832 social media posts from their respective development agencies, the study explores whether emerging donors advance alternative narratives of development cooperation or seek legitimacy through established frameworks and expectations. The second project, The Changing Architecture of Green Energy Assistance: A Network Analysis of Emerging Powers 2 , uses social network analysis of international green-technology assistance between 2012 and 2023 to examine whether emerging powers are reshaping established patterns of cooperation. events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. events.title: Shifting Boundaries: Perspectives on American Landscapes
events.address: Jefferson Drive at 12th St., SW, Washington, DC
events.description: American painters Willard Metcalf, Dwight Tryon, Winslow Homer, and Abbott Thayer created profoundly beautiful views of the New England landscapes where they lived and worked. These paintings largely depict that environment as timeless and static. Shifting Boundaries looks at these works from a new angle by engaging a multiplicity of voices and viewpoints to explore what these paintings can tell us about changes to this region both past and present. As Shifting Boundaries reveals, the views these artists created of pasturelands in Massachusetts and of seascapes in Maine were transforming even as these artists recorded them. This reshaping of landscapes has only accelerated in the century since Metcalf, Tryon, Homer, and Thayer depicted them. Shifting Boundaries pilots a new mode of collaborative curatorial practice. NMAA Lunder Curator of American Art Diana Greenwold , curatorial assistant Mary Mulcahy , and interpretation specialists Liz Gardner and Amy Freesun partnered with Lauren Brandes (Smithsonian Gardens), Dennis Chestnut (Groundwork Anacostia River DC), Jerome Foster II (Waic Up), Elizabeth James-Perry (Aquinnah Wampanoag artist), Lorette Picciano (Rural Coalition), Stephanie Toothman (National Park Service), and Melinda Whicher (Smithsonian Gardens) to develop the themes for this exhibition, select works of art, and write object labels. The group’s perspectives, drawn from their individual areas of professional expertise and their own personal experiences, allow us to see new details in these stunning works of art. The landscapes become invitations to explore a century of human impact on New England land and water, the erasure of indigenous histories, and the environmental changes that are altering this region today.

events.title: South Lakes Theatre Arts Presents Come From Away
events.description: Come From Away, written by Irene Sankoff and David Hein, is a critically acclaimed musical featuring a poignantly relevant script and a deeply moving score. The show’s global presence resonates across all audiences as an uplifting reminder of humanity’s ability to come together, no matter what the circumstances. Based on real events of September 11th, 2001, Come From Away tells the story in which 38 planes, carrying thousands of passengers from across the globe, were diverted to the isolated community of Gander, Newfoundland. The locals of the small town played host to the world as they fed, housed, and comforted the stranded passengers for over four days. Inundated by culture clashes and language barriers, the people of Gander persevered, demonstrating the power of kindness. On the 10 th anniversary of 9/11 in 2011, Sankoff and Hein traveled to Gander to interview residents and returning passengers. They turned hundreds of distinct accounts into a celebrated musical. For this 25 th anniversary year of September 11th, South Lakes Theatre Arts is honored to bring these accounts to life. Content Warning: Some mature content & langage. Disclaimer: There will be NO intermission for this production.

events.title: The American Story
events.description: The National Archives Museum debuts a once-in-a generation redesign of its permanent exhibits: The American Story and the Discovery Center - connecting visitors with the National Archives in revolutionary ways. The American Story will showcase items and records in the National Archives that tell important moments in our nation's history. Visitors will get up close to more than 40 original artifacts and documents, including a rare 1823 Stone Engraving of the Declaration of Independence, George Washington's annotated copy of the Constitution, and presidential gifts including horseshoes to President Bush from Queen Elizabeth II. The American Story will be the first and only museum in Washington, DC to use artificial intelligence (AI) to bring each visitor a special, individualized opportunity to explore the records of the American people and engage with American history. This exhibit brings more than two million historic records to life, offering a personalized journey through our nation's past. This new museum experience provides all Americans with a special opportunity to celebrate the 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence.

events.description: Friday, November 20th—Join us for Trans Day of Remembrance and Resilience (TDORR), a day of COMMUNITY POWER when we honor the memories of transgender people whose lives were lost in acts of violence this year. What is TDOR? From GLAAD : the first Transgender Day of Remembrance (TDOR) was started in 1999 by transgender advocate Gwendolyn Ann Smith as a vigil to honor the memory of Rita Hester, a transgender woman killed in 1998. The vigil commemorated all the transgender people lost to violence since Rita Hester’s death, and began an important tradition that has become the annual Transgender Day of Remembrance. In a 2012 article with Huffpost , Smith is quoted as saying, “the right to simply exist is first and foremost. With so many seeking to erase transgender people — sometimes in the most brutal ways possible — it is vitally important that those we lose are remembered, and that we continue to fight for justice.” Why the 2nd “R”? While not entirely widespread (yet), the MoCo Pride Family uses the moniker “TDORR” to underscore gratitude as essential to our celebration of transgender lives. On the Transgender Day of Remembrance, we honor those we have lost and those that continue to live in the face of violence, oppression, and all other forces turned against our community. Transgender people are brave — we will survive, and we will do so with our ancestors and martyrs in our hearts. events.title: Triangle Art Studios Presents “Luminance: Contained” by Susan Darrow
events.description: “Luminance Contained ” will feature black & white works by Rockville-based fine art photographer Susan Darrow. Darrow first picked up a camera in high school, learning old-school techniques of darkroom developing and printing. She uses a full-format digital camera with a large sensor to capture maximum sharp detail, and carefully composes the best possible photograph in-camera, minimizing post-production editing. Darrow is drawn to Black & White Photography because of the stability and order it brings to what was once a chaotic scene. “The tones are all connected to each other, and what was once a jostling combustion of color at once becomes peaceful.” The exhibition runs November 20 through December 27. Gallery hours are Fridays & Saturdays, 10am – 5pm; Sundays, 11am – 2pm. There will be an opening reception Saturday, November 21, 5 – 8pm. The exhibit will also be open for the Bethesda Art Walk on Friday, December 11, 6 – 8pm.

Led by Assistant Professor Clement Akpang, 59 students from four seminar courses offered between Fall 2024 and Spring 2026, conducted original research to deepen understanding of the university’s holdings and update how we interpret and exhibit these objects. The exhibition features 37 tangible heritage objects, ranging from an Egúngún Paaka from Yorubaland to a Kii [brass pipe], attributed to the Baumum people of Cameroon, accompanied by images and video that illuminate their rich histories. Research on the entire collection is presented in an accompanying illustrated publication. events.title: We Make History
events.description: As the nation commemorates 250 years since the signing of the Declaration of Independence, "We Make History" explores how history happens, is preserved and shared. In Washington, D.C. and places around the country, many people were quietly keeping the records, building the collections, and developing the skills that would create America’s historical narrative. These community-based stories serve as the building blocks for 250 years of American history. Using the country’s anniversary as a milestone, the museum uses its community driven practice to celebrate local civic engagement and encourage local history keeping. This exhibition is a tribute to celebrating our communities and making possible a better understanding of our shared past. These stories are important to marking the Semiquincentennial because they help show the legacy of how people make history one act, one document, one story at a time. By bringing these stories to the forefront in 2026, the exhibit inspires the next generation to keep and share their own stories and records to add to America’s historical narrative. We Make History has an anticipated opening date of May 30, 2026.

Just in time for America’s 250th anniversary, 1776 takes audiences inside the Continental Congress, where John Adams pushes for independence, Benjamin Franklin brings his wit and wisdom, and Virginia’s own Thomas Jefferson is called upon to put the revolutionary cause into words. The story also features Richard Henry Lee of Virginia, whose resolution calling for independence helped move the colonies toward a historic decision. What happens when a room full of passionate, stubborn and politically divided men try to agree on the future of a nation? There’s plenty of debate, a little scheming, larger-than-life personalities and some unforgettable music. With music and lyrics by Sherman Edwards and a book by Peter Stone, 1776 combines clever dialogue, colorful characters, political maneuvering and a memorable score. From the spirited opening number, “Sit Down, John,” to the lively “The Lees of Old Virginia” and the stirring “Is Anybody There?,” the music captures the humor, frustrations and high stakes behind the birth of a nation. Forget the dusty history books. 1776 presents the founding fathers as real people, with big egos, strong opinions, competing interests and a monumental decision to make. events.title: A Raisin in the Sun
events.description: The Younger family on Chicago’s South Side is holding tight to visions of a brighter future, but when a life insurance check arrives, suddenly possibility comes with a price. Sat Nov 21 2:00pm To – 4:30pm The Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center Buy Tickets Clarice website Add to Calendar “What happens to a dream deferred? / Does it dry up / like a raisin in the sun?” - Langston Hughes The Younger family on Chicago’s South Side is holding tight to visions of a brighter future. When a life insurance check arrives, suddenly possibility comes with a price. As each family member reaches for a different dream, they must confront what a better life really means – and what America is willing to share. Both tender and electrifying, A Raisin in the Sun celebrates Black joy, resilience and family while facing the brutal realities of segregation and discrimination. A landmark of American theater, it made history as the first Broadway play written by an African American woman (Lorraine Hansberry), the first Broadway play directed by an African American man (Lloyd Richards), and the first commercially produced Broadway drama to center Black life. TDPS Assistant Professor KenYatta Rogers (director of Stick Fly, Men on Boats , Metamorphoses and Home ) directs this enduring American classic. Location The Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center 8270 Alumni Drive College Pa

events.description: Arts Barn Stage Adventures is a performing arts series for children ages 6 and under, featuring live theatre, music, dance, puppetry, magic, and storytelling. In the Hollow Stump presented by Beech Tree Puppets, seven very different animals seek shelter from the winter cold and snow in a large hollow stump. The cuddly, hand-crafted rod-puppets will enchant any child as the characteristics of each animal are revealed through a unique and descriptive poem and song. When the animals let newcomers enter and the space inside the stump grows tighter, these songs interweave. Adapted from the popular tale, The Mitten, this tale celebrates community, as the animals learn to share one space. Gentle and sensory friendly. Join us afterward for a fun, hands‑on activity where kids can carve their own woodland creatures with scratch cards in the Arts Barn Gallery!

events.title: Autumn in Watercolor: A Fall Painting Workshop @ Lost Rhino Brewery
events.description: Spend a cozy fall evening slowing down, sipping, and exploring watercolor at Lost Rhino Brewery! This three-hour beginner-friendly workshop is designed to be a full creative experience, giving you the time to learn, experiment, and complete two fall-inspired paintings: a colorful birch tree landscape and a sweet pumpkin/ gourd “Thankful” card to take home. Led by a professional practicing artist and painter, you’ll be guided step-by-step while learning approachable watercolor techniques along the way. We’ll explore how to work with water and pigment, build layers, create texture, and embrace the beautiful, fluid nature of watercolor. No painting experience is needed, and there will be plenty of room to make each piece feel like your own. More than just leaving with two finished paintings, the goal of this workshop is to give you a foundation you can take with you. You’ll leave with new skills, a better understanding of watercolor, and hopefully a new creative outlet you can continue enjoying long after the class is over. All painting materials are included, plus each ticket includes a beverage from the bar to sip while you paint. Come settle in for three cozy hours of painting, learning, and creating something inspired by the season.

events.title: Christmas Ornaments from Nature (Parent & Child Workshop - Ages 6+)
events.address: 1851 McGuckian Street, Suite B, Annapolis, MD 21401
events.description: NOTE: This is a parent and child workshop, cost of a seat get you and one child into the workshop to make 2 ornaments together. Natural Christmas Ornament Workshop with Maria from Beaver Creek Cottage Garden Bring the beauty of the natural world to your holiday tree this season! In this festive hands-on workshop, Maria of Beaver Creek Cottage Garden will guide you through crafting a charming collection of handmade ornaments using materials straight from nature. You'll create an adorable snowman couple and a whimsical Christmas fairy — all made from natural materials like dried botanicals, seed pods, twigs, moss, berries, and more. Each piece is entirely one-of-a-kind, shaped by the unique textures and character of the natural materials you choose. The result is a set of heirloom-quality ornaments with a warmth and charm no store-bought decoration can match. DETAILS Recommended for ages 6-12. Each ticket covers one adult and one child. All materials provided. Space is limited — register early to secure your spot! MEET MARIA Maria has a BS degree in Biology from the University of Maryland plus an MS degree in Pharmacognosy from the University of Rhode Island. She founded Willow Oak Flower + Herb Farm over 40 years ago, which has been featured in Baltimore Bride, Washingtonian Weddings, Capitol Romance and Maryland Farm & Harvest. She taught at Tai Sophia (now known as Maryland University of Integrative Health) and Continuing Education at Anne Arundel Community College for over 30 years. Plants are her passion, and she hopes to share this joy with others through Beaver Creek Cottage Garden.

events.title: Cocoa, Cookies & Cows | A Highland Cow + Valais Sheep  Holiday Experience
events.description: Cocoa, Cookies & Cows | A Highland Cow + Valais Sheep Holiday Experience One of Scarlet Springs Farm’s most beloved holiday traditions is back! Cocoa, Cookies & Cows invites you to spend a festive afternoon with our adorable Highland cows, calves, Valais sheep, and lambs before warming up with homemade hot cocoa and cookies in our beautifully decorated Ridgetop Stable. Your experience begins with a 30-minute group animal immersion, where you’ll have the chance to pet, brush, feed, and love on our friendly Highland cows and calves, along with our famously puppy-dog-friendly Valais sheep and lambs. While the animals don’t mind sharing their barn, this portion of the experience will be largely outdoors, so please dress accordingly. After enjoying the highlands & lambs, we’ll clean up and then head down to the Ridgetop Stable, where you can warm up in our heated, enclosed space for the remaining hour while taking in the sweeping views of the farm. For the holidays, the stable will be transformed with festive décor and music to create the perfect cozy holiday setting. Settle in with your family, sip on homemade hot cocoa, enjoy a tower of delicious cookies, and soak up what makes Scarlet Springs so special. Before you head home, be sure to stop by The Scarlet Shop for Highland-inspired Christmas gifts and keepsakes. Whether this is your first visit or an annual family tradition, Cocoa, Cookies & Cows is the perfect way to slow down, get cozy, and make holiday memories together.​ ​What’s Included with Your Ticket: 1.5 hour experience on the beautiful 74-acre Scarlet Springs Far 30 minutes with the Highlands — pet, brush, feed, and meet our fluffy, friendly Highland cows and calves Time with our Valais sheep and lambs Seat with your party in our festive, beautifully decorated and heated Ridgetop Stable Homemade hot cocoa and cookies Sweeping views of the farm and a festive holiday atmosphere

events.title: Colonial Annapolis & Maryland State House
events.description: Follow your colonial-attired guide through Annapolis’s historic district, highlighting the 18th century, long considered the Golden Age of Annapolis. events.title: Fruition – Something More: The Final Tour
events.description: FRUITION’S FINAL TOUR As Fruition releases its eighth studio album, Something More, via Bloodshot Records, the acclaimed Americana band is also announcing plans to step away from touring following the scheduled tour dates, which now extend through January 2027. More than 15 years together, building a grassroots audience with stacked vocal harmonies and collaborative, song-driven Americana, this is American roots music at its broadest and boldest — a melting pot of rock, soul, folk, and pop. Produced by Grammy winner Tucker Martine (The Decemberists. My Morning Jacket), “...this album is the culmination of almost two decades of making music as Fruition,” explains Jay Cobb Anderson. Asked about the mission behind Something More, Kellen Asebroek shares: “We set out to show the world what we’ve learned along the way, both musically and personally, but perhaps more importantly, this album makes a point to be honest about the things we’ve had to UNLEARN. The truth of this album is found in kicking old habits, letting go of control, interrogating our motives, and approaching each session with fearless, open hearts.” Handmade Moments is a fearless, all-weather duo based in New Orleans, LA.

events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

This program is part of the Historic Grounds series, where scholarly research bridges with community dialogue. Each session pairs scholarly insight with discussion, offering a unique space to learn, reflect, and connect. Join Francesco De Salvatore, Director and Curator of the Alexandria Oral History Center, and descendants of the Frederick Douglass Memorial Cemetery (a historic African American burial ground) and the Colored Rosemont community (site of some of the first African American homeowners in Alexandria) as they discuss two community history initiatives being completed in Alexandria, Virginia. The afternoon unfolds as follows: 2:00 p.m. welcomes guests with subject matter expert exploration of local history and its national relevance, followed by spirited conversation over coffee and light refreshments. At 3:00 p.m., an exclusive experience tied to the day's topic offers specialized tours or vault access to rarely seen collection objects. Your ticket includes lecture and Q&A admission to the keynote presentation and interactive discussion; a copy of Freedom in the Age of Slavery: A History of Free People of Color in Virginia; vault access to rarely seen artifacts from the Woodlawn & Pope-Leighey House Collection; access to the Woodlawn estate for open house tours; and complimentary coffee and light refreshments. Francesco De Salvatore is a public historian, memory worker, and archivist committed to ethical, stakeholder-driven historical preservation. They founded and direct the City of Alexandria's Alexandria Oral History Center, a community-driven collaboration documenting and preserving Alexandria's stories and memories. Francesco holds an M.A. in History from the University of Illinois at Chicago and an M.A. in American Studies from Geor

events.title: Indecent: The True Story of a Little Jewish Play
events.description: ASL Sign Interpreted Performance and Afterword discussion on Friday, November 20 . Written by Paula Vogel, Score and Original Music by Lisa Gutkin and Aaron Halva Directed by Sasha Olinick Performances will be held in the Theatre Arts Arena on the Montgomery College Rockville campus. In 1906 a young, up and coming Jewish/Polish writer, Sholem Asch, penned “God of Vengeance”, a play attacking religious hypocrisy and lovingly depicting a romantic relationship between two women. The play quickly became a hit as it toured throughout Europe and was translated from its original Yiddish into several different languages. But in America, when an English translation opened on Broadway in 1923, the play was quickly shut down and the cast, director and producer were jailed and prosecuted for violating obscenity laws. Indecent, by Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright Paula Vogel, charts the history of this incendiary drama and the path of the artists who risked their careers and lives to perform it. INDECENT is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Dramatists Play Service. Indecent is recommended for mature audiences and teenagers aged 13 and older due to adult themes and historical prejudice.

events.title: Jean Rondeau
events.description: Back by popular demand, the extraordinary Jean Rondeau returns to dazzle CMM audiences with his singular command of the harpsichord. Described by The Washington Post as “a master of his instrument with the sort of communicative gifts normally encountered in musicians twice his age,” Rondeau is the most exciting harpsichordist of his generation. His program celebrates the golden age of French Baroque keyboard music: Louis Couperin’s improvisatory grandeur, Rameau’s sparkling brilliance, François Couperin’s elegant wit, and Royer’s thrilling La Marche des Scythes. In the resonant sanctuary of First Lutheran Church, this music will transport you straight to Versailles.

events.title: Jim Patton & Sherry Brokus
events.description: 1pm • No Cover • $10-$20 suggested donation Jim Patton & Sherry Brokus Jim Patton and his wife and musical collaborator, percussionist Sherry Brokus , have a gift for turning everyday moments into songs with deeper meaning. Their new album, Pattonville, on Berkalin Records, turns that gift toward the past, gathering tales from years gone by, told from a deeply personal perspective. The album reached #2 on the Folk DJ Charts in June 2026, and Goldmine Magazine's Lee Zimmerman calls each song "a singular standout, brimming with feeling, finesse and an unmistakable emotional bond." Critic Geoffrey Himes praises "the distinctive body of work the duo has created over four decades."Following the full-band rock 'n' roll of Two True Loves, Pattonville trades some of that energy for reflection, finding in old stories the roots of the present and the common ground we all share.

events.title: Liana Flores
events.description: Liana Flores' story is one of cultural cross-pollination, unlikely chances, and quite possibly a signpost for the evolution of folk music in the digital age. Raised in rural Norfolk pre-internet ubiquity, the bossa nova CDs belonging to Liana's Brazilian mother were a first glimpse into a musical world beyond Eleanor Rigby on cassette and Gilbert & Sullivan in the village hall. At 19, she went from building an early listener base with showtune covers in the YouTube era, to penning her own songs. The influences all started coming together, in self-recorded songs combining the harmonic stylings of bossa nova guitar with personal lyrics - often gloomy but persevering, expressing anxieties and depicting the nature in her hometown. Three years later, one of these unassuming songs, ‘rises the moon’, was uploaded to TikTok without the singer's knowledge and became a surprise hit, spawning countless cover versions before the labels came calling. Nearly a billion streams later, it's arguably a defining folk song of its generation. After signing to Verve Records, a full-length record, Flower of the soul, followed in 2024. events.description: Born in 1953 in Detroit, Michigan, Marshall Crenshaw learned to tune a guitar correctly at age ten and has been trying ever since. His first big break came in 1978 playing John Lennon in “Beatlemania”, first as an understudy in New York, then in the West Coast company, followed by a national touring company. Removing himself from that situation in Feb. 1980, Marshall settled in New York City. Enthralled by the hyper-diverse musical culture of the City, and the local Rock scene in particular, Marshall formed a Rock and Roll band with brother Robert on drums and Chris Donato on bass. Of his City Winery New York show last fall Infocus Visions Music & Arts Magazine hailed, “Marshall Crenshaw live is an experience in itself. Forget the solo artist; this is a full band explosion that showcases the magic of musical synergy. Watching them on stage is like peeking into a creative engine room. You see the interplay, the energy flowing between them, how each member feeds off the others to create that signature Marshall Crenshaw sound.”

events.title: Meet the Author: Mia Bear Is Finally Home – Children's Storytime & Crafts
events.description: Join Enough Adoption Foundation for a special children's book reading celebrating love, adoption, and the many ways families are formed. Enjoy an engaging story time followed by arts and crafts. Ideal for children ages 0–8. All families are welcome! Written by Mia Dickerson and her late mother, Margie Hampton, the story follows Mama Bear and Papa Bear as they prepare their home—and their hearts—for the arrival of their little girl, Mia. Through beautiful illustrations and gentle storytelling, children are introduced to adoption in a compassionate, age-appropriate way. As part of Enough's Adoption Literacy Program, this reading is more than story time. It's an opportunity to help children appreciate different family experiences, encourage kindness and understanding, and introduce language that helps adoptees feel seen, valued, and supported. Whether your family has been touched by adoption or you're simply looking to introduce your little one to the beauty of different families, all are welcome! Together, we're helping raise a generation of children who understand that families may be formed differently, but every child deserves to feel loved, worthy, and enough. Come read, learn, and celebrate belonging with us! Children must be accompanied by a parent or caregiver.

events.title: Miles Davis and John Coltrane Centennial
events.description: The year 2026 marks 100 years since the births of Miles Davis and John Coltrane, two visionaries of modern jazz. To mark the occasion, esteemed trumpeter and composer Terence Blanchard and saxophonist and composer Ravi Coltrane join forces for a centennial tribute celebrating the history, evolution, and continuing future of jazz. The two bandleaders bring distinct personal and artistic connections to this performance: Coltrane as the son of John Coltrane and Blanchard as one of today’s leading trumpeters, shaped by the music and innovation of Miles Davis. Together, they channel the creativity, freedom, and spirit of experimentation that defined Davis and Coltrane’s artistry. Rather than a nostalgic reenactment, the concert offers a reimagining grounded in the legacy of Davis and Coltrane while remaining anchored in the present. True to jazz’s essence, Blanchard, Coltrane, and their ensemble embrace improvisation, invention, and emotional intensity, allowing the music to evolve in the moment throughout the evening.

events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Opening Reception for "Luminance Contained"
events.description: “Luminance Contained ” will feature black & white works by Rockville-based fine art photographer Susan Darrow. Darrow first picked up a camera in high school, learning old-school techniques of darkroom developing and printing. She uses a full-format digital camera with a large sensor to capture maximum sharp detail, and carefully composes the best possible photograph in-camera, minimizing post-production editing. Darrow is drawn to Black & White Photography because of the stability and order it brings to what was once a chaotic scene. “The tones are all connected to each other, and what was once a jostling combustion of color at once becomes peaceful.” The exhibition runs November 20 through December 27. Gallery hours are Fridays & Saturdays, 10am – 5pm; Sundays, 11am – 2pm. There will be an opening reception Saturday, November 21, 5 – 8pm. The exhibit will also be open for the Bethesda Art Walk on Friday, December 11, 6 – 8pm.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: South Lakes Theatre Arts Presents Come From Away
events.description: Come From Away, written by Irene Sankoff and David Hein, is a critically acclaimed musical featuring a poignantly relevant script and a deeply moving score. The show’s global presence resonates across all audiences as an uplifting reminder of humanity’s ability to come together, no matter what the circumstances. Based on real events of September 11th, 2001, Come From Away tells the story in which 38 planes, carrying thousands of passengers from across the globe, were diverted to the isolated community of Gander, Newfoundland. The locals of the small town played host to the world as they fed, housed, and comforted the stranded passengers for over four days. Inundated by culture clashes and language barriers, the people of Gander persevered, demonstrating the power of kindness. On the 10 th anniversary of 9/11 in 2011, Sankoff and Hein traveled to Gander to interview residents and returning passengers. They turned hundreds of distinct accounts into a celebrated musical. For this 25 th anniversary year of September 11th, South Lakes Theatre Arts is honored to bring these accounts to life. Content Warning: Some mature content & langage. Disclaimer: There will be NO intermission for this production.

events.description: 2026 marks the centennial of two visionary architects of modern jazz: Miles Davis and John Coltrane. To celebrate their enduring legacy, two of today’s most innovative and influential bandleaders—Terence Blanchard and Ravi Coltrane—will join forces for a series of exceptional concerts. Blanchard and Coltrane, both deeply connected to the spirit and lineage of these jazz icons, embody the very essence of creativity, futurism, transcendence, freedom—and the timeless “birth of cool” that defined Miles and Trane’s artistry. This centennial tribute will not be a nostalgic reenactment, but a bold reimagining. Each concert will be a living, breathing experience, rooted in the legacy of Davis and Coltrane, yet fully anchored in the now. True to jazz’s essence, the performances will embrace improvisation, invention, and emotional intensity, ensuring that every evening is unique and unrepeatable. A powerful celebration of heritage, transmission… and the future of jazz.

events.description: Beatrix Farrand is considered the first commercially successful woman landscape architect in the United States. Dumbarton Oaks Park in Georgetown is one of her lasting legacies. Meet at the Dumbarton Oaks Park sign on R St. NW between 31 st St. NW and Avon Pl. NW. Walk may be cancelled in the event of bad weather at the discretion of park staff. A group of soldiers decide to test the loyalty of the wives left behind at home, unleashing a cruel and reckless chain of events that have devastating consequences. What begins as drunken bluster soon spirals into an act of irreversible violence, exposing the destructive power of pride, entitlement and unchecked authority. At the center of the tragedy is Lucretia, a woman whose integrity becomes the focus of both admiration and devastating cruelty. Written by Britten in the aftermath of the World War II, The Rape of Lucretia reflects a society struggling to rebuild itself after immense suffering and moral collapse. Britten’s chamber opera confronts the abuse of power with unflinching boldness while searching for compassion, redemption and the possibility of renewal. events.title: Triangle Art Studios Presents “Luminance: Contained” by Susan Darrow
events.description: “Luminance Contained ” will feature black & white works by Rockville-based fine art photographer Susan Darrow. Darrow first picked up a camera in high school, learning old-school techniques of darkroom developing and printing. She uses a full-format digital camera with a large sensor to capture maximum sharp detail, and carefully composes the best possible photograph in-camera, minimizing post-production editing. Darrow is drawn to Black & White Photography because of the stability and order it brings to what was once a chaotic scene. “The tones are all connected to each other, and what was once a jostling combustion of color at once becomes peaceful.” The exhibition runs November 20 through December 27. Gallery hours are Fridays & Saturdays, 10am – 5pm; Sundays, 11am – 2pm. There will be an opening reception Saturday, November 21, 5 – 8pm. The exhibit will also be open for the Bethesda Art Walk on Friday, December 11, 6 – 8pm.

events.title: Weekend Unwind: Sound Bath + Reiki : Saturday Mornings in Falls Church
events.address: 7777 Leesburg Pike, Ste 204S, Falls Church, VA 22043
events.description: Most people start their Saturday with a list. Groceries, errands, the thing they didn't finish on Friday, still buzzing around in their head. By the time they've “relaxed,” it's Sunday night. Weekend Unwind flips that. Eleven o'clock, one hour, lying down. Crystal singing bowls, a short guided meditation, and Reiki, in a small room with ten people in it and no agenda at all. Nothing to achieve, nothing to be good at. You just lie there and let the week drain out of your shoulders. This class has a different feel from our Thursday night one. Thursday is about switching off. Saturday is slower. People arrive less wound up, settle in faster, and tend to float out rather than rush out. Several regulars come as their standing Saturday thing, the way other people have a standing brunch. It pairs well with brunch afterwards, for the record. If you've never been to a sound bath: you keep your clothes on, you lie on a mat under a blanket, you close your eyes, and I do the rest. The bowls are played around and near you, the sound is physical as much as it is musical, you feel it in your chest, and an hour passes faster than you expect. Everything is provided. Show up in something comfortable with ten minutes to spare, and that's the whole preparation. I'm Victoria Vita. I've been a CPA for over twenty years and a healer for more than seven, and I teach every one of these classes myself. When you come back, and most people do, it's the same room, the same bowls, and the same person. That sameness is kind of the point. Rated 5.0 from 32 Google reviews. Guests mention the warm welcome, feeling comfortable from the first visit, and booking again — that's the Saturday I try to run. What's included: • 60 minutes of crystal singing bowls, guided meditation and Reiki • Mat, blanket and bolster provided... just bring yourself • Ten spots only, so the room stays quiet and unhurried • A slow finish... no one is hustled out the door at noon Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: Camelot
events.description: Welcome to CAMELOT! Borrowing from the Arthurian legends, CAMELOT is Lerner and Loewe's fantastical masterpiece. An idealistic King Arthur hopes to create a kingdom built on honor and dignity, embodied by his Knights of The Round Table. He establishes an order built on using “might for right.” His ideals, however, are tested when his lovely queen, Guenevere, falls in love with his most loyal knight, Lancelot. Add in the dastardly Mordred and his wicked schemes and it soon appears this dream of a kingdom may only exist for one brief, shining moment. ​ This stirring Golden Age musical has enchanted generations of theatregoers with its sweeping score and iconic characters. It is a romance, a tragedy, a comedy, an adventure, a fantasy, and a stirring exploration of power and leadership all at once. And above all, it is a piece about the stories and ideals we pass along to future generations.​

events.description: Join professional textile conservators at Woodlawn for a unique, hands-on preservation workshop! From Quilts to Keepsakes opens with a 45-minute presentation by RB Textile Conservation exploring expert conservation strategies and a behind-the-scenes look at the preservation of Woodlawn’s own Quaker signature quilt. Then, attendees are invited to apply these expert techniques to their own history. Bring a small- to medium-sized personal textile and learn museum-approved handling, folding, and packing methods. You will leave with the confidence and materials to safeguard your family heirlooms for generations! Best of all, proceeds from this workshop directly fund our next vital textile conservation project, Mary Eliza Angela Lewis Conrad’s wedding dress. About the speakers: Rebecca Beyth Stern is the founder and conservator at RB Textile Conservation. Stern previously worked at the US Holocaust Memorial Museum, Cooper Hewitt, Smithsonian Design Museum and The Metropolitan Museum of Art. Stern holds a master’s degree in textile conservation from The Fashion Institute of Technology and a bachelor's degree in art conservation from The University of Delaware. She is a Professional Member of AIC. Recent notable projects include a Ruth Bader Ginsberg Judicial Robe, a Playboy Bunny assemble, several textiles from the Thomas Edison National Historic Park, NPS and several textiles for the 250th Celebrations at the Smithsonian Institution. Kayla Silvia-Winokurzew currently serves as an Assistant Conservator at RB Textile Conservation. She holds a B.A. in Anthropology and a B.S. in Art with a concentration in Art History, alongside minors in Chemistry and Apparel & Textiles, all from the State University of New York at Oneonta. She earned a MPhil in Textile Conservation from the Centre for Textile Conservation at the University of Glasgow in Scotland. events.address: 30 W. Potomac St., Ste 102, Brunswick, MD 21716
events.description: This November Full Beaver Supermoon rises with a steady, grounding energy, symbolizing resilience, creation, and laying strong foundations for the future. Traditionally linked to a time of building and preparing for winter’s stillness, it reflects a period of securing what matters most and reinforcing both inner and outer stability. Spiritually, it encourages you to nurture your sense of home, protect your energy, and commit to the structures that support your growth. Beneath its luminous glow, we’re reminded to tend to what sustains us, release instability, and move forward with quiet strength and purpose. Our Full Moon Gatherings offer a supportive space to connect in community, move gently, and settle into meditation while clarifying intentions for the next lunar cycle. Through accessible practices such as Extra Gentle and Restorative Yoga, a deeply immersive sound bath, and other rituals, we honor the full moon as a time of release, clarity, and renewal - celebrating our own fullness while opening to the wisdom of what is yet to unfold. No previous yoga experience required.

events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

events.title: Indecent: The True Story of a Little Jewish Play
events.description: ASL Sign Interpreted Performance and Afterword discussion on Friday, November 20 . Written by Paula Vogel, Score and Original Music by Lisa Gutkin and Aaron Halva Directed by Sasha Olinick Performances will be held in the Theatre Arts Arena on the Montgomery College Rockville campus. In 1906 a young, up and coming Jewish/Polish writer, Sholem Asch, penned “God of Vengeance”, a play attacking religious hypocrisy and lovingly depicting a romantic relationship between two women. The play quickly became a hit as it toured throughout Europe and was translated from its original Yiddish into several different languages. But in America, when an English translation opened on Broadway in 1923, the play was quickly shut down and the cast, director and producer were jailed and prosecuted for violating obscenity laws. Indecent, by Pulitzer Prize-winning playwright Paula Vogel, charts the history of this incendiary drama and the path of the artists who risked their careers and lives to perform it. INDECENT is presented by arrangement with Concord Theatricals on behalf of Dramatists Play Service. Indecent is recommended for mature audiences and teenagers aged 13 and older due to adult themes and historical prejudice.

events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. events.title: Piper Jones Band at the Old Brogue
events.description: Old Brogue Irish Pub welcomes the Piper Jones Band on Saturday, November 22nd, 2026 in Great Falls, Fairfax County, Virginia. The Piper Jones Band brings spirited, magical dance tunes and songs to everyone—from Celtic music veterans to those hearing it for the first time. Frances Cunningham, EJ Jones, and Andrew Toy form a lyrical, high-energy trio built on the moving and beautiful sounds of Highland bagpipes, accompanied by unique percussive chords from the bouzouki. While maintaining a strong musical base in traditional tunes from Ireland, Scotland, and Appalachia, the group performs original instrumental compositions and powerful vocal harmonies. The band steps off stage from time to time to lead the audience in traditional dances, creating an interactive, celebratory evening. This performance combines authentic Celtic traditions, dynamic musicianship, and community participation in Fairfax County, Virginia. Admission is $25 plus tax per performance; full six-concert season tickets are $135 plus tax. Piper Jones Band delivers spirited energy, masterful instrumentation, and the joy of traditional Celtic music. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.description: Please join us at St. Alban’s Episcopal Church for our second Muldoon Memorial Concert of the season! The Carmina and Illuminare Early Music Vocal Ensembles will perform this concert on St. Cecilia’s Day, the traditional feast of the patron saint of music and musicians. Carmina is a vocal chamber ensemble dedicated to bringing the exquisite beauty of early music to the Washington, DC community. The program will feature motets honoring Cecilia herself, alongside music that celebrates singing, music-making, and the extraordinary human impulse to make music together. The concert also marks the debut concert of the ensembles' new artistic director, Dr. Mark Helms. Come join Carmina and Illuminare for a joyful opportunity to reflect on why we sing, and why music has held such a powerful place in our lives for centuries. Stay for the festive reception. The concert is sponsored by the St. Alban's Muldoon Concert fund and is free. For more information, contact the St. Alban’s Church office at 703-256-2966, or Adam Detzner, Minister of Music and Organist, at adetzner@stalbansva.org .

Continuing the delicious tradition of last season’s Brahms and Ice Cream and Mozart and Cookies concerts, Sweet Hearts Patisserie will offer a variety of complimentary macarons and other French pastries after the performance—the perfect finish to a musical treat.

events.title: The Lutheran Seminary in the Battle of Gettysburg
events.description: On July 1, 1863, the Civil War came to the Seminary's door, leaving in its wake countless stories of heroism and horror. The Lutheran Theological Seminary moved to the western side of Gettysburg in 1832, followed three decades later by national debates that tore apart the United States and divided the institution. As the Battle of Gettysburg opened on July 1, 1863, the Civil War came to the Seminary's door, leaving in its wake hundreds of wounded soldiers, thousands of dollars of property damage, and countless stories of heroism and horror. Explore the social, military, and medical impacts on this critical site through a brief history of its stories and legacies. Codie Eash serves as Director of Education and Interpretation at Seminary Ridge Museum and Education Center in Gettysburg, where he has served several roles as a member of the staff since 2012. In 2014, he earned a bachelor’s degree in communication/journalism from Shippensburg University of Pennsylvania, where he also completed a minor in History. In 2024, Codie began working on a master’s in American History at Gettysburg College through The Gilder Lehrman Institute of American History. In addition to Museum tours and programming, he lectures for American Battlefield Trust conferences, National Park Service sites, historical societies, Civil War roundtables, educational groups, and other organizations. Codie is a founding contributor to Pennsylvania in the Civil War , reviews books for Civil War Monitor and Emergin

events.description: The Maryland Opera Studio presents Benjamin Britten’s haunting chamber opera that centers on the tragic consequences when power and pride collide. Sun Nov 22 3:00pm To – 5:30pm The Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center Buy Tickets Clarice website Add to Calendar Maryland Opera Studio performs Benjamin Britten’s The Rape of Lucretia , an emotionally raw chamber opera that's tragic plot begs us to reflect on violence, misogyny, the abuse of power and how these themes continue to haunt society. A group of soldiers decide to test the loyalty of the wives left behind at home, unleashing a cruel and reckless chain of events that have devastating consequences. What begins as drunken bluster soon spirals into an act of irreversible violence, exposing the destructive power of pride, entitlement and unchecked authority. At the center of the tragedy is Lucretia, a woman whose integrity becomes the focus of both admiration and devastating cruelty. Written by Britten in the aftermath of the World War II, The Rape of Lucretia reflects a society struggling to rebuild itself after immense suffering and moral collapse. Britten’s chamber opera confronts the abuse of power with unflinching boldness while searching for compassion, redemption and the possibility of renewal. events.title: Triangle Art Studios Presents “Luminance: Contained” by Susan Darrow
events.description: “Luminance Contained ” will feature black & white works by Rockville-based fine art photographer Susan Darrow. Darrow first picked up a camera in high school, learning old-school techniques of darkroom developing and printing. She uses a full-format digital camera with a large sensor to capture maximum sharp detail, and carefully composes the best possible photograph in-camera, minimizing post-production editing. Darrow is drawn to Black & White Photography because of the stability and order it brings to what was once a chaotic scene. “The tones are all connected to each other, and what was once a jostling combustion of color at once becomes peaceful.” The exhibition runs November 20 through December 27. Gallery hours are Fridays & Saturdays, 10am – 5pm; Sundays, 11am – 2pm. There will be an opening reception Saturday, November 21, 5 – 8pm. The exhibit will also be open for the Bethesda Art Walk on Friday, December 11, 6 – 8pm.

events.title: Ghostwoman
events.description: There is no reason for GHOSTWOMAN’s fourth album to exist. Welcome to the Civilized World is born to a broken world; a corrupt inheritance – Evan Uschenko and Ille van Dessel are under no illusions about its futility – and yet, this thing is alive. It’s an allergic reaction to the times we are living in: a welt that screams to be itched, the purging of a modern sickness they could no longer stomach. Beyond rationality, this record came from a place of gut feeling and a lack of any other option. Hell may have cracked wide open – but GHOSTWOMAN will not go quietly. GHOSTWOMAN itself only exists because Uschenko and van Dessel were the ones “stupid enough to commit to it”. Conceived by Uschenko after cutting his teeth as a touring multi-instrumentalist, the project was brought to life in an abandoned farmhouse in Diamond City, Alberta. There, for two months, he would make the self-released, self-titled debut album which was produced and dubbed directly to custom-made cassette tapes. The music has always been beautifully inhospitable, earned only by those curious enough to seek it out. events.description: Modern classics don’t come any bigger than Les Misérables, and Olney Theatre celebrates it for the first time in honor of the show’s 40th anniversary. Based on Victor Hugo’s sweeping 19th-century novel of redemption, revolution, and love, the songs of Les Miz conquered Broadway in the 1980s and continue to resonate in this third decade of the 21st Century. Follow Jean-Valjean from his beginnings as convict #24601 to life in hiding, to protector of Cosette, pursued all the while by the relentless Javert, culminating in the revolutionary passions of the 1832 Paris uprising. Join us at the barricade this holiday season, and be stirred by a musical unmatched by its lyrical humor, its calls for justice, and its portrayal of the sacrifices one can make in the name of love. Featuring: Kevin S. McAllister as Javert, Alex De Bard as Eponine, Tracy Lynn Olivera as Madame Thénardier, Jordan Friend as Thénardier, Stephanie Waters as Fantine, Ben Clark as Marius, and more to be announced soon.

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

A bold, tour-de-force comedy that leaves it all on the mat! Audience Advisories: strong language, simulated violence/fighting, racial stereotypes, flashing lights and haze effects. The 2nd Sunday matinee of the run will be a mask required performance. Please bring a mask or one will be provided to you.
