events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: Les Misérables-Olney Theatre
events.description: Modern classics don’t come any bigger than Les Misérables, and Olney Theatre celebrates it for the first time in honor of the show’s 40th anniversary. Based on Victor Hugo’s sweeping 19th-century novel of redemption, revolution, and love, the songs of Les Miz conquered Broadway in the 1980s and continue to resonate in this third decade of the 21st Century. Follow Jean-Valjean from his beginnings as convict #24601 to life in hiding, to protector of Cosette, pursued all the while by the relentless Javert, culminating in the revolutionary passions of the 1832 Paris uprising. Join us at the barricade this holiday season, and be stirred by a musical unmatched by its lyrical humor, its calls for justice, and its portrayal of the sacrifices one can make in the name of love. Featuring: Kevin S. McAllister as Javert, Alex De Bard as Eponine, Tracy Lynn Olivera as Madame Thénardier, Jordan Friend as Thénardier, Stephanie Waters as Fantine, Ben Clark as Marius, and more to be announced soon.

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

Come for the 30-minute lesson, then stay to put your new moves into practice on the Hank Dietle’s dance floor! No partner needed.

Guests are welcome to conquer our steep .5 mile driveway OR take a longer climb on The Trails - a 3.5 mile wooded loop through the property (sorry, there’s a steep hill on this one too!). Either way, you’re sure to earn the libations waiting for you in the Taproom! There will be beer-mosas, Great Country Farms apple cider donuts, and grub from The Truck at the top to refuel after your workout. Consider it the perfect warm-up for Thanksgiving Dinner. We’ll be pouring drinks at 9am, and The Truck will be opening at 10am with food items! Don't forget to purchase an event tee shirt while you're shopping in the taproom! To keep all of our climbers safe, the Dirt Farm Driveway will be CLOSED to all traffic during this event. Guests will be directed to the Dirt Farm parking lot via Bluemont Vineyards driveway - please follow the signage leading up the hill to find your way to DFB! We highly recommend carpooling for this event as parking can be limited. We have primarily outdoor seating, so be sure to dress for the outdoors and bring a blanket and beanie to keep toasty warm! Come for the climb, but stay the day! Happy Hour starts at 3:00 p.m. and taps are open 'till 4:45pm…it’s a perfect way to gather with the ones you love and keep the family entertained while they’re in town! Climb, Beer, Turkey, Nap! events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

Race points count toward the Year-Long 5K, 10K, and Back of the Pack Series, as well as the Sippin Series. A virtual race option is also available. Registration is $35 for the 5K and $50 for the 10K through October 31st, with a $5 increase on race morning. Packet pickup and race-day registration are available at the event; arrive about an hour early. This Turkey Trot combines scenic trail running, Civil War history, and community spirit in Fairfax County, Virginia. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: Mental Reset: Sound Bath + Reiki : Thursday Evenings in Falls Church
events.address: 7777 Leesburg Pike, Ste 204S, Falls Church, VA 22043
events.description: Thursday is a weird day. The week isn't over, but you are. Mental Reset is one hour at the end of the workday where nobody needs anything from you. You come in, you lie down on a mat, you get a blanket and a bolster, and for the next sixty minutes your only job is to listen. I play crystal singing bowls, guide you through a short meditation so your mind has something to do besides replay the day, and offer Reiki while you rest. Most people tell me some version of the same thing afterward: the noise in their head finally turned down. Not off: down. Enough that they can go home and actually be home, instead of answering emails in their head at the dinner table. You don't need experience. You don't need to know how to meditate, and you definitely don't need to “clear your mind.” If you could do that, you wouldn't need this class. First-timers are in the room most weeks. There are ten spots. That's deliberate. It's a small room, I can see everyone in it, and it never feels like an event. It feels like an exhale. A few regulars started as skeptics; more than one of our Google reviews comes from someone who arrived doubting the whole thing and left surprised at how settled they felt. You don't have to believe in anything for an hour of sound and rest to do you some good. Run by Victoria Vita: CPA for 20+ years, healer for 7+. I sat behind a desk with a brain that wouldn't switch off for a long time before I found this work. Thursday nights are built for the person I used to be. Rated 5.0 from 32 Google reviews. Come straight from work. Leave like the week let go of you first. What's included: • 60 minutes of crystal singing bowls, guided meditation and Reiki • Mat, blanket, and bolster everything is here; you bring nothing • Small group: 10 people maximum, same teacher every week • Time at the end to sit up slowly, have water, and not rush out Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: A Christmas Story - Goose Creek Players
events.description: Step into the nostalgic world of holiday magic, childhood dreams, and laugh-out-loud family fun with A Christmas Story, brought to life on stage by Goose Creek Players, Inc.! Based on the beloved holiday classic, A Christmas Story follows nine-year-old Ralphie Parker on his quest for the ultimate Christmas gift: an official Red Ryder BB gun. But between his mother's warnings that he'll "shoot his eye out," his father's hilarious battles with the family furnace, a department store Santa, and the unforgettable leg lamp, Ralphie's Christmas adventure is anything but ordinary! Filled with memorable characters, heartwarming moments, and plenty of holiday hilarity, this charming stage adaptation captures the wonder, excitement, and occasional chaos of Christmas through the eyes of a child. Join us for a delightful holiday tradition that will have audiences of all ages laughing, reminiscing, and celebrating the spirit of the season. Don't miss this Christmas classic brought to life on stage — it's the perfect holiday outing for the whole family! Performances at Franklin Park Performing & Visual Arts Center, 36441 Blueridge View Lane, Purcellville, VA 20132: Fri Nov 27 7:30 PM; Sat Nov 28 2:00 PM & 7:30 PM; Sun Nov 29 2:00 PM; Fri Dec 4 7:30 PM; Sat Dec 5 2:00 PM & 7:30 PM; Sun Dec 6 2:00 PM. Tickets $24-$25: https://goosecreekplayers.com/tickets/

events.title: A Sherlock Carol
events.description: A Sherlock Carol , a play with carols, by Mark Shanahan inspired by the works of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, is an inventive holiday production that seamlessly intertwines the worlds of Sherlock Holmes and A Christmas Carol. Set in 1894, the story reimagines a grown-up Tiny Tim who seeks out the famed detective to investigate the mysterious death of Ebenezer Scrooge. Holmes is compelled to confront his own past and inner turmoil, guided by spectral encounters reminiscent of Scrooge’s transformative journey. Combining aspects of two classics of Victorian literature and uniting them both in a joyful mug of holiday cheer, this play is a festive feast for the senses. Recommended for ages 6 & up.

events.description: Alfredo Mojica is a cornerstone of the DC salsa community. Born in Central America, he is a consummate percussionist and vocalist who began performing at a tender age with such legends in the field as Celia Cruz, Eddie Palmieri, Willie Colón, Dizzy Gillespie, Buddy Rich, El Gran Combo, Ray Barretto, and others. Watching Alfredo move flawlessly between timbales, congas, or bongos while belting out salsa classics in his own amorous and heart-jolting style is quite a thing to behold. He is joined on the Bossa stage every Friday night by an ebullient and first-class roster of musicians, sure to have you breaking a sweat on the dance floor with salsa, bachata, merengue, and more. events.title: Black Friday Hike at Dirt Farm Brewing
events.description: Skip the chaos of the crowds and join us for a breath of fresh mountain air this Black Friday! Trade the shopping lines for scenic views and spend the day unwinding on The Trails at Dirt Farm Brewing. Wander through the woods, soak in the crisp mountain air, and then cozy up in the Taproom with one of our warm seasonal drinks and hearty food specials from the kitchen. It’s the perfect way to slow down, reconnect with nature, and embrace the peaceful side of the holiday weekend. The Trails will be open for hiking from 11am-4pm for your Black Friday hike and the Taproom will be open from 12-9pm. Stick around and be one of the first to take a walk on the Christmas Trail at Dirt Farm! From 5-8pm guests can see the mountain illuminated by thousands of holiday lights and festive photo ops at this kick-off to the holiday season! Guests are welcome to enjoy a stroll through the forest where you can find whimsy, merriment and endless amounts of holiday cheer at this holiday light display! Immerse yourself in a winter wonderland, and enjoy nostalgic scenes as you wander through the Blue Ridge Mountains. Learn more and get your tickets to The Christmas Trail at Dirt Farm here: https://dirtfarmbrewing.com/event/the-christmas-trail-at-dirt-farm-brewing/2026-11-27/ Whether you’re coming out from Washington D.C., Alexandria, Arlington, or Baltimore, or you’re just cruising over from Round Hill, Purcellville, Clarke County, or Winchester, we’re always glad to welcome friendly faces here in Bluemont—near or far. Our community stretches across the region, and nothing makes us happier than sharing good beer, great food, and even better company with all of you right here in Loudoun County, Virginia!

events.title: Christmas Traditions by Candlelight at the William Paca House
events.description: Gather your family and friends and experience the joy of the holiday season with a festive tour of the William Paca House! On this guided candlelit tour, explore holiday traditions that have evolved over time and discover how families in Annapolis and Maryland celebrated the holiday season in generations past. Learn how the Paca household prepared to welcome friends and guests for the holidays. At the conclusion of the tour, enjoy a sweet treat, and a take-home recipe to help bring a taste of the past to your own holiday celebrations. Note: This tour will be offered on a range of dates and times in November and December. To see times, visit our November and December event calendar . Cost: $15 General Admission. $12 for Historic Annapolis members and Military. Interested in a private version of this tour for your group of 10 or more? Contact Cara Garside, Visitor Services Manager, at grouptours@annapolis.org . Accessibility Considerations : Accessing the interior of the William Paca House requires ascending and descending several flights of stairs. Cancellation and Refund Policy : Historic Annapolis reserves the right to cancel or alter any programs. Unless otherwise stated, all tickets are non-refundable. Photography Policy : Historic Annapolis reserves the right to take photographs and video footage of people of all ages at Historic Annapolis-sponsored events for publicity. If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please opt out by notifying Historic Annapolis staff. Food Allergy Notice: Food samples will be provided at this program. Some samples may contain gluten and nuts , and cross-contact may occur. Participants with any food allergies or dietary restrictions should use their best judgment before participating and do at their own risk.

events.title: Crazy Chester - A Very Carrboro Tribute To The Band & The Last Waltz 50th Anniversary Tour w/ JP Hudson
events.description: Crazy Chester Formed in early 2020 for a series of one-off events in the piedmont region of North Carolina, Crazy Chester is a homegrown tribute act to The Band, consisting of Carrboro musicians Jones Bell (Mellow Swells, Ravary), Charles Cleaver (Big Star's Third, Fancy Gap, Lemon Sparks), Rob DiMauro (Heat Preacher, Mixtape Grab Bag, One After 919), Justin Ellis (Slow Teeth, Ravary, Easter Island, One After 919), and Rafael Green (solo artist, Ravary, One After 919), respectively recreating and playing the parts of Richard Manuel, Garth Hudson, Levon Helm, Rick Danko, and Robbie Robertson. For the sixth year in a row, Crazy Chester will be performing most of The Band's legendary farewell performance from Thanksgiving Day 1976, immortalized in the 1978 Martin Scorsese film "The Last Waltz" - complete with additional musicians and special local guests to play the songs originally performed in the film by Joni Mitchell, Bob Dylan, Neil Young, and many more. But this time - they're taking the show on the road to celebrate 50 Years of The Last Waltz. A show that must be seen to be believed. Full list of guest performers TBD!

events.title: Cult of Love-Round House Theatre
events.description: Celebrate the holidays with the Broadway sensation Cult of Love ! In this gripping, music-filled play, four adult siblings (and their partners) return home for Christmas Eve, carrying secrets, resentments, and competing ideas of what family demands. As the singing and celebration give way to confrontation, old wounds reopen and new revelations emerge. Leslye Headland’s “stormy, compassionate, [and] cuttingly observant” ( TimeOut NY ) play interrogates the complexity of family loyalty, the power of religion, and what it truly means to love one another.

events.title: Gallery B Presents “Intersections | Realism & Abstraction”
events.description: “ INTERSECTIONS ⎸ Realism & Abstraction” is a group exhibition featuring four artists – Lawrence Chandler, Angela Iovino, Ariana Progri, and Ravi Raman – with distinct art styles in conversation with each other, showing that even the most realistic art is a form of abstraction (a reduction of reality) and that abstract art can hold elements of structural, grounded reality. Instead of treating realism and abstraction as binary opposites, works in the exhibition also intersect both worlds, showcasing how different artists navigate the spectrum between the two styles. Viewers not only will see realistic figures and recognizable subjects dissolving into, or emerging from abstract backgrounds, but also the use of bold brushstrokes, form, color, and textures to convey emotion rather than literal details.

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: Triangle Art Studios Presents “Luminance: Contained” by Susan Darrow
events.description: “Luminance Contained ” will feature black & white works by Rockville-based fine art photographer Susan Darrow. Darrow first picked up a camera in high school, learning old-school techniques of darkroom developing and printing. She uses a full-format digital camera with a large sensor to capture maximum sharp detail, and carefully composes the best possible photograph in-camera, minimizing post-production editing. Darrow is drawn to Black & White Photography because of the stability and order it brings to what was once a chaotic scene. “The tones are all connected to each other, and what was once a jostling combustion of color at once becomes peaceful.” The exhibition runs November 20 through December 27. Gallery hours are Fridays & Saturdays, 10am – 5pm; Sundays, 11am – 2pm. There will be an opening reception Saturday, November 21, 5 – 8pm. The exhibit will also be open for the Bethesda Art Walk on Friday, December 11, 6 – 8pm.

events.description: 8 Ohms Band is a horn heavy funk band from Annapolis, Maryland. Since 2007, they've been bringing their unique blend of funk, soul, pop, reggae, and R&B to stages across the DMV and beyond — sharing the stage with legends including Earth Wind & Fire, P Funk and Chuck Brown. With three studio albums under their belt — including 2021's critically acclaimed "Nineteen" — the band has been featured in the Washington Post, BBC Radio 6, and are three-time Rammie Award winners for Best Show of the Year (2023, 2024 & 2025), Wammie Award and Maryland Music Award winners. Whether it's a festival stage, a wedding, or a sweaty club gig, 8 Ohms delivers real instruments, real energy, and a real good time.

events.title: Christmas in the Capital: Annapolis Traditions and State House Trees
events.description: Welcome the holidays with Watermark's Christmas in the Capital Tour: Annapolis Traditions and State House Trees. Meet your period-attired guide inside our cozy office before embarking on your tour. Stroll with your colonial guide around Maryland’s capital city, trimmed in greenery for the season. Hear holiday traditions of times past and present as you walk by colonial mansions, Victorian homes, and quaint shops A highlight of the tour is the Maryland State House, with decorated Christmas trees representing the different counties of Maryland, presented by the Federated Garden Clubs of Maryland. The tour ends at Annapolis's grand Christmas tree at Market House Park. Take home the holiday cheer with a goody bag of treats including George Washington’s famed eggnog recipe!

events.title: Christmas Traditions by Candlelight at the William Paca House
events.description: Gather your family and friends and experience the joy of the holiday season with a festive tour of the William Paca House! On this guided candlelit tour, explore holiday traditions that have evolved over time and discover how families in Annapolis and Maryland celebrated the holiday season in generations past. Learn how the Paca household prepared to welcome friends and guests for the holidays. At the conclusion of the tour, enjoy a sweet treat, and a take-home recipe to help bring a taste of the past to your own holiday celebrations. Note: This tour will be offered on a range of dates and times in November and December. To see times, visit our November and December event calendar . Cost: $15 General Admission. $12 for Historic Annapolis members and Military. Interested in a private version of this tour for your group of 10 or more? Contact Cara Garside, Visitor Services Manager, at grouptours@annapolis.org . Accessibility Considerations : Accessing the interior of the William Paca House requires ascending and descending several flights of stairs. Cancellation and Refund Policy : Historic Annapolis reserves the right to cancel or alter any programs. Unless otherwise stated, all tickets are non-refundable. Photography Policy : Historic Annapolis reserves the right to take photographs and video footage of people of all ages at Historic Annapolis-sponsored events for publicity. If you do not wish to be photographed or filmed, please opt out by notifying Historic Annapolis staff. Food Allergy Notice: Food samples will be provided at this program. Some samples may contain gluten and nuts , and cross-contact may occur. Participants with any food allergies or dietary restrictions should use their best judgment before participating and do at their own risk.

events.title: Echoes of Time in Rock Creek Park Guided Hike
events.description: The Milkhouse Ford trail offers both beautifully forested nature and a glimpse into Washington DC’s history. Ramble with a ranger for a guided hike on this 1.7-mile loop, where you will encounter 5000 years of history, from traces of Indigenous land usage, to Fort DeRussy (which saw action during the Civil War), to the two-room log cabin used by poet Joaquin Miller, and to the historic Milkhouse Ford river crossing (one of Rock Creek Park’s oldest and most well-preserved fords). Meet at the Rock Creek Park Nature Center, bring plenty of water, dress for the weather, and be prepared for a fun and enjoyable outing.

Our knowledgeable guides will provide insights into the fort’s construction, its role in defense, and the stories of those who lived and served here. events.title: Improv Church
events.description: The Vine presents Improv Church, a unique comedy experience that gathers community for laughter, storytelling, and connection on select dates in 2026 from 7:00 p.m. to 8:30 p.m. at 2501 Gallows Road in Dunn Loring, Fairfax County, Virginia. This is improv comedy that takes place in a church—literally. The pastor, an improv comedian who has performed across the country, gives the monologue that kicks off the show. Improv Church celebrates the belief that the church is the gathered people of God—all of us. Improv is about connection and telling stories while highlighting the joy, failures, and foibles of real life. The Bible is full of those stories too, creating a cool opportunity to gather and enjoy legitimate improv comedy while exploring the intersection of faith and real life in community. Laughing together is good for the church and for people with no interest in the church—just come, it's good. This is a completely improvised comedy show featuring off-color language and scenarios with no restrictions on the comedians. The human condition can be hilarious as can a well-placed word. Ages 14+. Admission is $10. Improv Church combines comedy, community, faith exploration, and authentic human connection in Fairfax County, Virginia. Contact: vine2501@gmail.com / (703) 573-5836. For dates and information, visit thevineva.org. Discover More Attractions in #FXVA

events.title: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power
events.description: Necessary Means: Adreinne Waheed on Gathering and Power, an exhibition examining the beauty, dynamism, and political force of collective Black life across the African Diaspora through the photography of Howard alumna Adreinne Waheed. Curated by Kathryn Coney-Ali, executive director of the Howard University Gallery of Art, and Dr. Melanee C. Harvey-Fryar, associate professor of art history in the Chadwick A. Boseman College of Fine Arts, the exhibition brings Waheed’s documentary street photography into conversation with selections from the Waheed Photo Archive. Together, the works explore Black joy, protest, community, cultural tradition, and the power created when people gather. Necessary Means opens Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at the Howard University Museum in Founders Library and remains on view through May 28, 2027.

events.title: Research & Enrichment! Science with Your Dog
events.description: Join the GW Dog Lab for fun, free enrichment with your dog! The GW Canine Cognition Collaborative (aka GW Dog Lab) is a student-run lab in the Anthropology Department. Research sessions are on campus, after hours and on weekends, and are designed to last only 1 hour. Because humans and dogs share an environment, we can learn a lot about the way that environment has shaped our species by comparing dog and toddler cognition. We play simple games with dogs designed to measure their cognition and then compare them to toddlers. How to Participate 1. Start by submitting a pre-screening form. This helps us learn about your dog 2. Next, open your email and look for your onboarding information sent from canine.cognition@gwu.edu. 3. Then, using the information in your email, sign up for your initial visit. This is a get-to-know-you visit that makes it easier for dogs to get acclimated to our testing space. 4. Finally, after the initial visit, depending on your dog's comfort level, you will get email invitations to studies your dog is eligible for! Parking information can be found on the GW Dog Lab website.

events.title: SILENT FILM Series: Wings (1927)
events.description: Soar into the spectacle and emotion of Wings , the first film to ever win the Academy Award for Best Picture. Set against the backdrop of World War I, this drama follows two young fighter pilots whose rivalry, friendship, and love for the same woman unfold amid the danger and excitement of aerial combat. Featuring astonishing flight photography and large-scale action sequences that still inspire and awe nearly a century later, Wings combines thrilling adventure with heartfelt human drama. STARS: Clara Bowm Richard Arlen, Charles Rogers, Gary Cooper RUNTIME: 114 Minutes GENRE: Silent, Action, Drama, Romance, War RATING: PG-13 This show is part of the Silent Film Series , celebrating timeless scores and classic films. When the lights go down and the Mighty Wurlitzer rises from the orchestra pit, audiences are treated to a live organ performance featuring Tedde Gibson—complete with a short musical set before the credits roll and a brief introduction to each silent film. Our beloved Wurlitzer turns 100 this December, having filled the theater with music for nearly a century. The Weinberg Center , located in the heart of Downtown Frederick, MD, offers a historic backdrop for a unique film experience.

events.title: The Grateful Allman Band Experience
events.description: 9pm • $20 • On Eventbrite The Grateful Allman Band Experience Celebrating the Summer of Love All Year Long! The music of The Grateful Dead, The Allman Brothers Band, and The Band The Grateful Allman Band Experience (GABE) celebrates the music of the Grateful Dead, the Allman Brothers Band, and the Band—three legendary acts united by the spirit of the iconic Watkins Glen Summer Jam. Featuring musicians from Mid-Atlantic favorites Danger Bird, Covered with Jam, Montgomery Warlocks, and the Crimestoppers, GABE delivers an improvisation-driven show built on adventurous jams, musical chemistry, and timeless songs. For more than a decade, GABE has entertained audiences from the Carolinas to New Jersey, with multiple recent sellouts drawing crowds of 200–350+. This isn’t a costumed tribute act—it’s a celebration of the feel, freedom, and interplay that made these bands legendary, welcoming jam-band devotees and casual fans alike. For venues, GABE offers three passionate fan bases in one compelling broader promotional reach, a multigenerational audience, and a proven draw.

events.description: Christmas…Tuba-style Merry Tubachristmas® will celebrate its 52nd year. Created by Harvey Phillips, Merry Tubachristmas® 2026 concerts will be presented in over 300 cities throughout the United States and in several foreign countries. Tubachristmas® is an annual event created to honor Dr. Harvey G. Phillips’ teacher, mentor, friend, and associate, the late great tubist William J. Bell. Every Tubachristmas® performance features traditional Christmas carols especially arranged by American composer Alec Wilder. Through Wilder, Tubachristmas® concerts pay tribute to composers who have embraced these noble instruments with solo and ensemble compositions. It’s no wonder why the warm toned, smooth organ sounds of the tuba-euphonium choir has won the ears and hearts of every audience, making a Tubachristmas® concert an established Christmas tradition in cities throughout the world Learn more about Tubachristmas® at their official website .

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape.Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available.Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape.Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available.Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: Go beyond King Street on a 90-minute guided walk through Alexandria's remarkable Wilkes Street Cemetery Complex—13 historic cemeteries, 52 acres, and more than 35,000 burials in one walkable landscape. Led by independent historian and cemetery superintendent David Heiby, creator of Gravestone Stories, the tour connects Alexandria's past to the American Revolution, War of 1812, Civil War, Cold War, and more. Meet George Washington's pallbearers, Revolutionary War patriots, Civil War soldiers, a Soviet spy, and others whose stories illuminate more than two centuries of Alexandria history. Every stop is grounded in original research, cemetery records, and discoveries made within the complex, including graves rediscovered after nearly 200 years. Tours are limited to small groups. The 90-minute walk covers approximately 1 to 1.5 miles over historic cemetery paths and uneven terrain. Free parking is available. Tours are offered Fridays and Saturdays at 1:00 p.m., with an additional Thursday tour at 3:30 p.m. Tickets are $30 per person and include the official Gravestone Stories companion e-book. See the Gravestone Stories website for current availability and booking.

events.description: The Blackbyrds performing this special concert on Thanksgiving weekend to celebrate 50 years since the release of “Rock Creek Park”, a classic song that has endured for generations! The band is one of the most successful ever from the DC area and came together in the 1970s as Howard University students under the guidance of their music professor, the late great jazz trumpeter Donald Byrd who became their manager and producer. They created a unique jazz funk sound combined with soulful harmonies that made a big impact on the music charts. The Blackbyrds’ biggest hit songs were “Walking In Rhythm”, their Grammy nominated million selling smash hit on both the R&B and pop charts; “Happy Music”, an uplifting party anthem that was their biggest R&B hit; and “Rock Creek Park”, their beloved song known for its infectious groove and famous verse “doin’ it in the park, doin’ it after dark, oh yeah…Rock Creek Park!” The Blackbyrds tour around the world but always look forward to performing in the DC area where they are most appreciated. The band’s original core members as well as new members are all from the DC area led by drummer Keith Killgo. Their crowd pleasing performance features all of their most popular songs plus those by Donald Byrd including “Places And Spaces” and “(Fallin’ Like) Dominoes.” SATURDAY, NOV 28. 2026 Dinner & Doors 6:00pm Showtime 8:00pm
